'''Gusto, Inc.''' is a [[San Francisco]]-based company that develops payroll, benefits, and human resource management software for businesses based in the United States.

== History ==
ZenPayroll was part of [[Y Combinator (company)|Y Combinator]]'s Winter 2012 batch.<ref name=pando-dec-2012>{{cite news|url = http://pando.com/2012/12/11/zenpayroll-raises-ycs-largest-seed-round-from-the-mt-rushmore-of-valley-entrepreneurs/|title = ZenPayroll raises YC's largest seed round from the Mt. Rushmore of Valley entrepreneurs|last = Carney|first = Michael|date = December 11, 2012|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[PandoDaily]]|archive-date = March 1, 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210301195344/https://pando.com/2012/12/11/zenpayroll-raises-ycs-largest-seed-round-from-the-mt-rushmore-of-valley-entrepreneurs/|url-status = dead}}</ref> The company raised $6.1 million from investors including Box CEO and co-founder [[Aaron Levie]], [[Yammer]] CEO and co-founder [[David O. Sacks]], and others.<ref name=pando-dec-2012 /><ref name=techcrunch-dec-2012 /><ref>{{cite news|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/venturecapital/2012/12/11/paychecks-move-to-the-cloud-as-google-salesforce-back-zenpayroll/|title = Paychecks Move to the Cloud as Google, Salesforce Back ZenPayroll|last = Gage|first = Deborah|date = December 11, 2012|accessdate = January 20, 2015|newspaper = [[Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref> The service launched officially on December 11, 2012 in [[California]]<ref name=pando-dec-2012 /><ref name=techcrunch-dec-2012>{{cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2012/12/11/zenpayroll-launches-cloud-based-payroll-service-with-6-1m-in-seed-funding-from-the-ceos-at-yammer-box-yelp-and-dropbox/|title = ZenPayroll Launches Cloud-Based Payroll Service With $6.1M In Seed Funding From CEOs At Yammer, Box, Yelp And Dropbox|last = Williams|first = Alex|date = December 11, 2012|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[TechCrunch]]}}</ref> by Joshua Reeves, Tomer London and Edward Kim.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garfinkle |first=Allie |date=March 10, 2024 |title=Three founders launched HR software unicorn Gusto – then their moms hit it off |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/three-founders-launched-hr-software-115341841.html?guccounter=1 |access-date=October 15, 2026 |website=[[yahoo! finance]]}}</ref>

On June 12, 2013, the company announced support for paying contract workers and ensuring tax compliance through [[Form 1099]] and other forms. The company also announced plans to launch services in [[Florida]], [[Texas]], and [[New York (state)|New York]] state.<ref name=techcrunch-june-2013>{{cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2013/06/12/zenpayroll-now-gives-employers-a-way-to-pay-contractors-that-adp-cant/|title = ZenPayroll Now Gives Employers A Way To Pay Contractors That ADP Can't|last = Williams|first = Alex|date = June 12, 2013|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[TechCrunch]]}}</ref><ref name=pando-june-2013>{{cite news|url = http://pando.com/2013/06/12/zenpayroll-adds-support-for-contract-workers-preps-for-expansion-to-florida-texas-and-soon-new-york/|title = ZenPayroll adds support for contract workers, preps for expansion to Florida, Texas, and soon New York|last = Carney|first = Michael|date = June 12, 2013|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[PandoDaily]]|archive-date = January 13, 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210113070816/https://pando.com/2013/06/12/zenpayroll-adds-support-for-contract-workers-preps-for-expansion-to-florida-texas-and-soon-new-york/|url-status = dead}}</ref>

In August 2013, Gusto announced that it had exceeded $100 million in payments processed annually, and was launching in [[Florida]], [[Texas]], and [[Washington (state)|Washington]] state.<ref>{{cite news|url = http://pando.com/2013/08/29/zenpayroll-crosses-100m-in-payroll-processed-annually-launches-in-texas-florida-and-washington/|title = ZenPayroll crosses $100M in payroll processed annually, launches in Texas, Florida, and Washington|last = Carney|first = Michael|date = August 29, 2013|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[PandoDaily]]|archive-date = January 12, 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210112173605/https://pando.com/2013/08/29/zenpayroll-crosses-100m-in-payroll-processed-annually-launches-in-texas-florida-and-washington/|url-status = dead}}</ref> In September 2014, the company announced its [[application programming interface]] (API) and partnerships with over a dozen [[small and medium business]] (SMB) back-office service companies.<ref>{{cite news|url = http://pando.com/2014/09/03/zenpayroll-aims-to-unite-the-smb-back-office-integrates-with-a-dozen-other-cloud-based-systems/|title = ZenPayroll aims to unite the SMB back-office, integrates with a dozen other cloud-based systems|last = Carney|first = Michael|date = September 3, 2014|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[PandoDaily]]|archive-date = January 20, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150120212702/http://pando.com/2014/09/03/zenpayroll-aims-to-unite-the-smb-back-office-integrates-with-a-dozen-other-cloud-based-systems/|url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/09/03/zenpayroll-api/|title = ZenPayroll Partners With A Dozen Other SMB Back-Office Tools|date = September 3, 2014|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[TechCrunch]]|last = Lawler|first = Ryan}}</ref> In December 2014, the company announced support for letting companies match employees' charitable donations.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://venturebeat.com/cloud/zenpayroll-now-lets-companies-match-employees-charitable-donations|title = ZenPayroll now lets companies match employees' charitable donations|last = Novet|first = Jordan|date = December 16, 2014|access-date = January 20, 2015|work = [[VentureBeat]]}}</ref> At the time, it was valued at over $100 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/02/19/cloud-based-payroll-app-zenpayroll-raises-20m-from-general-catalyst-and-kleiner-at-a-100m-plus-valuation/|title = Cloud-Based Payroll App ZenPayroll Raises $20M From General Catalyst And Kleiner At A $100M-Plus Valuation|last = Rao|first = Leena|date = February 19, 2014|accessdate = January 20, 2015|work = [[TechCrunch]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/venturecapital/2014/02/19/san-francisco-startup-zenpayroll-raises-20m-finds-novel-ways-to-lure-workers/|title = San Francisco Startup ZenPayroll Raises $20M, Finds Novel Ways to Lure Workers|last = Gage|first = Deborah|date = February 19, 2014|accessdate = January 20, 2015|newspaper = [[Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref>

In 2014,''[[VentureBeat]]'' listed the company among the best back-office software for small businesses.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://venturebeat.com/business/the-best-back-office-software-for-small-businesses|title = The best back-office software for small businesses|last = Grant|first = Rebecca|date = January 27, 2014|access-date = January 20, 2015|work = [[VentureBeat]]}}</ref> At the time, the ''[[New York Times]]'' compared the company to larger payroll processors such as [[ADP, LLC|ADP]], citing both advantages and disadvantages.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://bits.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/09/03/zenpayroll-gives-small-business-the-tech-tools-of-big-business/?_r=0|title = ZenPayroll Gives Small Business the Tech Tools of Big Business|last = Hardy|first = Quentin|date = September 3, 2014|accessdate = January 20, 2015|newspaper = [[New York Times]]}}</ref>

In July 2015, the company announced that it had expanded its business and opened a new office in [[Denver]], [[Colorado]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/business/ci_28549056/hickenlooper-google-backed-zenpayroll-plans-hire-1-750|title = Google-backed ZenPayroll plans to hire 1,750 people in Denver|date = July 28, 2015|accessdate = January 20, 2015|newspaper = [[Denver Post]]|last = Wallace|first = Alicia}}</ref> In September 2015, it was announced that ZenPayroll had changed its name to Gusto<ref>{{Cite web |last=Buhr |first=Sarah |date=2015-09-17 |title=ZenPayroll Is Now Gusto, Adds Benefits To Take On Zenefits |url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/09/17/zenpayroll-is-now-gusto-adds-benefits-to-take-on-zenefits/ |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>, and was broadening its focus to integrate health benefits and workers' compensation into its payroll software.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://venturebeat.com/business/zenpayroll-changes-its-name-to-gusto-starts-offering-insurance-workers-compensation|title = ZenPayroll changes its name to Gusto, starts offering insurance, workers' compensation|last = Novet|first = Jordan|date = September 17, 2015|access-date = September 26, 2015|work = [[VentureBeat]]}}</ref>  In December 2015, Gusto raised $50 million in funding and reached a $1 billion valuation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/williamalden/gusto-is-valued-at-1-billion-in-new-funding-round#.uhJP0el5kz|title = Gusto Is Valued At $1 Billion In New Funding Round|date = December 21, 2015|accessdate = January 20, 2015|publisher = [[BuzzFeed]]|last = Alden|first = William}}</ref>

''[[Venture Beat]]'' reported that Gusto was raising prices on all customers in October 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=Yeung |first=Ken |title=Gusto raising prices for all customers of its payroll service, starting October 1 |date=August 10, 2016 |work=[[VentureBeat]] |url=https://venturebeat.com/business/gusto-raising-prices-for-all-customers-of-its-payroll-service-starting-october-1}}</ref>

In July 2019, Gusto raised $200 million at a $3.8 billion valuation.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/donnafuscaldo/2019/07/24/gusto-amasses-3-8-billion-valuation-with-latest-fundraising-round/#761090a52820|title = Gusto Amasses $3.8 Billion Valuation With Latest Fundraising Round|date = July 24, 2019|accessdate = August 29, 2019|magazine = [[Forbes]]|last = Fuscaldo|first = Donna}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Gusto is now offering pieces of its service to other companies via API|url=https://techcrunch.com/2021/06/30/2171608/|access-date=2021-07-21|website=TechCrunch|date=30 June 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref> That year, the company announced the opening of its third office, in [[New York City]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SMB payroll startup Gusto raises $200M Series D, plans R&D expansion to NYC|url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/07/24/smb-payroll-startup-gusto-raises-200m-series-d-plans-rd-expansion-to-nyc/|access-date=2021-07-21|website=TechCrunch|date=24 July 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2023, the company was valued at $9.6 billion and had an annual revenue of $500 million.<ref name="Wilhelm" /> It had raised over $746 million in funding from investors as of 2024.<ref>{{cite web|last=Garfinkle|first=Allie|title=Gusto is cash flow positive–and it got there by sticking to mom-approved values|url=https://fortune.com/2024/05/10/gusto-cash-flow-positive-cofounders-mom-approved-values/|website=Fortune}}</ref> It currently develops payroll processing software, in addition to software for employee onboarding (work authorization forms, direct deposit forms, employee information aggregation). Separately, Gusto also provides employee [[health insurance]], [[dental insurance]], and vision insurance enrollment and administration. The company provides other employee-benefit and related products through third parties, including [[401(k)|401K]] and [[workers' compensation]] insurance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gusto.com/product/payroll|title=Gusto|website=Gusto|language=en|access-date=2018-07-10}}</ref>

In August 2025, Gusto announced it would acquire [[Guideline (company)|Guideline]], a startup providing [[401(k)]] retirement plans to small businesses, for approximately $600 million — Gusto's largest acquisition to date.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/08/27/gusto-retirement-guideline-deal.html|title=Gusto agrees to buy retirement plan provider Guideline|date=August 27, 2025|publisher=CNBC|access-date=2026-03-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/01/sources-gusto-paid-600m-to-acquire-guideline-plans-to-divest-customers-linked-to-rivals/|title=Sources: Gusto paid $600M to acquire Guideline, plans to divest customers linked to rivals|date=October 1, 2025|publisher=TechCrunch|access-date=2026-03-31}}</ref>

In April 2026, Gusto acquired Mosey, a startup that helps businesses comply with multi-state payroll and employment regulations, for an undisclosed amount.<ref name="axios-gusto-mosey-2026">{{Cite news|url=https://www.axios.com/pro/fintech-deals/2026/04/09/gusto-acquires-mosey-compliance-startup|title=Gusto acquires compliance startup Mosey|date=April 9, 2026|access-date=May 14, 2026|work=Axios}}</ref> By early 2026, Gusto had surpassed $1 billion in annual revenue, placing it alongside competitors Deel and Rippling in the $1 billion revenue tier, while maintaining a lower valuation of $9.3 billion based on a June 2025 employee tender offer.<ref name="tc-gusto-1b-revenue-2026">{{Cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/07/gusto-hits-1b-revenue-a-figure-that-brings-it-closer-to-public-markets/|title=Gusto hits $1B revenue, a figure that brings it closer to public markets|date=May 7, 2026|access-date=May 14, 2026|work=TechCrunch}}</ref>
